question: What is the primary function of the external female reproductive organs?

options.D: Nourish a growing baby during pregnancy

explanation: The external genitalia act as a physical barrier to shield delicate internal reproductive tracts from pathogens and trauma. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is it important for you as a nurse to understand female reproductive anatomy?

options.A: To prescribe hormonal contraceptives without a doctor
options.B: To diagnose sexually transmitted infections by sight alone
options.C: To accurately assess health problems and provide patient care
options.D: To perform surgical procedures independently in the clinic

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your anatomy helps you spot when something isn't quite right, chat easily with your patients, and guide them through different stages of life with confidence. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which external structure is a small, highly sensitive erectile organ?
explanation: The clitoris sits at the top of the labia minora and contains many nerve endings for sexual sensation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main function of the Bartholin glands?

options.B: Protect the pubic bone from physical shock
options.C: Secrete lubricating mucus into the vestibule
options.D: Produce eggs during the monthly cycle

explanation: Bartholin glands sit beside the vaginal opening and produce mucus to keep the mucosal surface moist. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h2)

question: What are the folds inside the vaginal wall that allow for stretching called?
explanation: Rugae are ridges of muscle and mucous membrane that let the vaginal canal expand greatly during birth and intercourse. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why is the normal acidic environment of the vagina important?

options.A: It softens the hymen before puberty
options.B: It prevents harmful bacteria from growing
options.C: It speeds up the movement of sperm cells
options.D: It helps the cervix open during labor

explanation: Normal vaginal acidity creates a hostile home for bad bacteria and yeast, protecting the reproductive tract from infections. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which layer of the uterus is shed monthly during menstruation?
explanation: The endometrium is the inner lining that builds up with blood and nutrients, then sheds if pregnancy does not occur. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h4)

question: A woman in labor is having strong contractions. Which part of her uterine wall is doing all that hard work?
explanation: Spot on! The myometrium is made of tough, powerful smooth muscle designed to push the baby safely into the world. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h4)

question: Where does fertilization of the egg by a sperm cell usually take place?

options.B: Inside the main cavity of the uterus
options.C: On the outer surface of the ovary

explanation: The wider ampulla section of the fallopian tube provides the right space and environment for the sperm to meet and fertilize the egg. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the role of the fimbriae at the end of the fallopian tubes?

options.A: Catch the released egg from the ovary
options.C: Secrete mucus to block foreign bacteria
options.D: Anchor the uterus to the pelvic wall

explanation: Fimbriae are fringe-like fingers that wave over the ovary at ovulation to sweep the egg inside the fallopian tube. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h5)

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries?

options.C: Pump blood through the pelvic floor
options.D: Produce eggs and secrete sex hormones

explanation: Ovaries serve as both glands that make hormones (estrogen and progesterone) and storage sites for female eggs. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which part of the ovary holds the developing egg follicles?
explanation: The outer layer, or cortex, contains ovarian follicles in different stages of growth and maturation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which main artery supplies blood directly to the uterus?
explanation: The uterine artery, branching from the internal iliac artery, brings oxygen-rich blood directly to the uterine walls. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why do you need to understand how the lymphatic system drains the reproductive organs?

options.A: It explains how menstrual cramps travel down to the legs
options.B: It shows how vaginal pH changes during a bacterial infection
options.C: It dictates the correct dosage for oral contraceptive pills
options.D: It helps track how pelvic cancers can spread through the body

explanation: Exactly! Cancer cells can hitch a ride through lymph vessels to nearby lymph nodes, so knowing these pathways is super important for staging and treatment. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h7)

question: A patient tells you she feels a heavy dragging sensation in her pelvis after having three children. What structures are likely stretched or weakened?

options.A: The Bartholin glands located near the vaginal opening
options.B: Ligaments and pelvic floor muscles supporting the uterus
options.C: The fimbriae at the ends of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The fallopian tubes where fertilization usually occurs

explanation: You're doing great! When pelvic floor muscles and support ligaments get stretched over time, they can lead to uterine prolapse, causing that heavy, dragging feeling. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse would typically do regarding female reproductive health?

options.A: Surgically repairing damaged uterine tissue during a caesarean section
options.B: Educating patients on normal menstrual cycles and warning signs
options.C: Recognizing signs of infection or inflammation in the vaginal canal
options.D: Assisting physicians or midwives during a routine pelvic physical exam

explanation: Spot on! Performing surgery is for doctors and surgeons—your core nursing superpowers include assessing, educating, and supporting patients every step of the way. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h8)
